slides.text:
A loop repeats a block of code. Go has a single loop keyword, `for`, and it takes several shapes: a counter, a condition, nothing at all, or a walk over a value.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
repeat while the condition holds
    do this
    maybe skip to the next lap
    maybe stop the loop early

slides.text:
Three sessions:

- **Session 1:** the counter, the condition, the loop with no end and `break`
- **Session 2:** `range`, `continue` and loops inside loops
- **Session 3:** counting down, two variables, labels and `switch` inside a loop

The classic `for` has three parts. The first runs once before the loop, the second is checked before every lap, and the third runs after every lap.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
Keep only the condition and the loop runs while it is true. Keep nothing and it runs until a `break` stops it.

slides.text:
`range` walks over a value. Over a number it counts from 0 up to one less than that number. Over a string it gives each character with its position.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
for each position and character
    of the text
        use them

slides.text: `continue` skips the rest of the current lap and starts the next one. `break` ends the whole loop, but only the innermost one when loops are nested.

slides.text:
A loop can count down, and it can hold two variables in its setup and its step.

A **label** names a loop. `break label` and `continue label` act on that loop, not only on the innermost one.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
outer: for each row
    for each column
        if done
            stop outer
        if skip
            next lap of outer

slides.text: A `break` inside a `switch` ends only the switch, even when the switch sits in a loop. To leave the loop from there, break to the label of the loop.

exercises.title: Count down and meet in the middle
exercises.guide: Count down, then move two variables in one loop.

chunks.guide: A loop can count down: start high, test with `>` and step with `i--`.

notes.text: Takes one off after every lap.

chunks.guide: Print a line after the loop.
The setup and the step can hold two variables each. They move toward each other until the condition fails.

notes.text: Both change together, in one statement.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `continue` skips only the print. `laps` already grew on every lap, and the step `i++` still runs, so odd laps count but print nothing.

exercises.title: Break out of both loops
exercises.guide: Name the outer loop with a label and leave it from inside.

chunks.guide: A label is a name followed by a colon, placed before a `for`. `break outer` ends the loop with that name, not just the innermost one.

chunks.guide: `continue outer` abandons the inner loop and starts the next lap of the loop named `outer`. A plain `continue` would only skip the inner lap.

notes.text: The inner loop is dropped, the outer one goes on.

exercises.guide: A `break` in a switch inside a loop, and the label that leaves the loop.
